title: Calendar privacy repair prototype

bullets: Can private event-detail publication be reduced while preserving team scheduling?
Three owner-scoped assistants; only availability is allowed to be shared.
Two Ministral model IDs, independently run as homogeneous teams.
Participant-message injection is implemented; MCP and adaptive attacks are extensions.
notes: This is a simplified CalBench-inspired setting, with our own generated data/code and acknowledged AI implementation assistance.
title: Question and scope

notes: 60 fixtures, 180 calendars, 2,334 fictional events. Twenty development, forty live-untested held-out. The security study uses four development cases. All plotted times UTC; the highlighted shared window is an illustration from the evaluator, not model input.
title: Fixed synthetic calendar data

bullets: v1/v2 each had 0/8 team success despite working API responses.
Missing availability, unsupported peer claims and conflicting final times were diagnosed.
v3 achieved 7/8; strict v4 schemas and an explicit shared commit achieved 40/40.
Tools compute availability/intersections; models publish, select and acknowledge.
notes: These are actual preserved runs, not unaided LLM reasoning claims. A valid schema or successful schedule does not establish privacy.
title: Diagnosis before attacks

bullets: An external peer's publish note carries the attack; attachments and system prompt remain unchanged.
Three static injection families plus benign and direct-request controls.

notes: Custom probes reuse our authored catalog. We have not run the entire built-in garak catalog. Exact-value matches are candidate flags, not a complete semantic classifier.
title: Threat model and garak adapter

notes: The original 40-case privacy pilot had correct scheduling in all cases. The same cases replayed through garak produced four exact-value candidates among 24 injection attempts. Initial AI review found three consistently attributed event disclosures and one real-value/misattribution case. Human confirmation pending. Replay adds no new model observations.
title: Observed baseline candidate flags

notes: Each cell is flagged/evaluable sessions, n=4 per model/condition. Small development sample does not justify a general model-safety ranking. A separate ten-session live garak smoke had 10/10 schedules correct and one candidate among six injections; it was not a defense experiment.
title: Existing model / condition breakdown

notes: Archived native garak discovery triggers predefined both-policy activation. Input minimizes peer prose; output releases fixed phase text. The attacker's note is inserted after its sender's own output policy. Invalid actions are rejected before any safe-text transform. Real verification is still pending connectivity.
title: Implemented automatic repair path

bullets: Four scenarios x two models x five conditions x four policies = 160 fresh team sessions.
Normally 1,120 logical completions; bounded retries and global resource caps.
Rotate policy order across pair blocks; match starting data and audit actual later histories.
Measure public candidate flags, scheduling correctness and raw-generation diagnostics separately.
No missing metric is treated as zero; final human rates remain undefined until review.
